A downloaded lecture's audio is dropped, the Settings storage figure falls to zero and stays there across a restart, and with the network gone the app goes back to the network for the very file it had cached — the row falls to the failed state instead of still claiming the lecture is on the device.

steps.action: Kill the network, restart the app and play the lecture from the Home queue.
steps.expected: Storage in use is still 0 MB, the app re-requests the audio file it had cached, and the row falls to the failed state rather than claiming the lecture is available offline.

173.title: A failed boot-locale chunk still launches a usable app

173.preconditions: Offline boot with locale=ru, clean user DB, onboarding already completed; every request for the ru locale chunk is aborted.

steps.expected: The app mounts anyway: URL /tabs/home with the bottom tab bar visible — not a blank WebView.

steps.action: Navigate to the Settings tab.
steps.expected: The screen renders and the interface-language row is readable (English fallback copy, not raw translation keys).

183.description: Offline, Pro. The archive schedule offers a 'Never' entry and the radio group reflects what is stored rather than filling in a default — turning the feature off used to leave the sweep deleting.

184.title: At the storage limit: the queue stays silent, the tap is answered
184.description: Offline, with the download limit set below one lecture. The background queue must refuse silently — its toast used to fire on every launch of a library already at the cap — and the refused row must render like any other queued lecture, with no badge of its own (the crossed-out cloud added by #1681 was never asked for; see #1744). 184.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db; settings.downloadLimitBytes preseeded to 1 MB.

steps.action: Add a lecture whose size the budget cannot fit.
steps.expected: It is added to the queue.

steps.action: Open Home and look at the row and the screen.
steps.expected: The row renders as a plain queued lecture — no crossed-out cloud and no failure icon — and no toast was shown.

steps.expected: The lecture is downloaded despite the limit: the storage figure in Settings stops reading zero.

185.title: A cancelled download releases the track, so it can be added again
185.description: Offline. A transfer is hung, the track cancelled mid-download, then the same lecture added again. Before the settle fix the cancelled promise was never resolved, so the track in-flight slot stayed occupied and the second add silently joined the abandoned transfer without ever asking for the file. The guard is that the re-add really reaches the network and finishes.
185.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db; the audio route hangs until the spec releases it.

steps.action: Add a lecture whose audio transfer never responds.
steps.expected: The row is queued and shows download progress.

steps.action: Delete the row from the queue while the transfer hangs.
steps.expected: The track leaves the playlist.

steps.action: Add the same lecture again, with audio now served.
steps.expected: It is added to the queue, a fresh transfer is requested, and the lecture reaches the downloaded state.

steps.action: Open Home.
steps.expected: The lecture is queued again under its own row.

186.title: A failed download says so, and a deliberate retry is always answered
186.description: Offline, with the audio route aborting so every transfer fails. The failure must surface as a notice rather than only a red X on a row nobody is watching, and the queue's rate-limit must never suppress the answer to something the user just pressed.
186.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db; the audio route aborts every request.

steps.action: Add a lecture whose audio cannot be fetched.
steps.expected: It is added and the transfer starts.

steps.action: Wait for the transfer to fail.
steps.expected: A notice names the failure and the row shows the failed state.

steps.action: Dismiss the notice.
steps.expected: No toast is on screen.

steps.action: Press 'Download again' in the track sheet.
steps.expected: The failure is reported again immediately, despite the queue cooldown.

187.title: A silent CDN costs seconds: the download hedges to a live region
187.description: Offline, with a two-region config. The preferred region accepts the audio request and never answers — the shape a dead region actually takes. The walk must not park on it: the other region is asked and serves the bytes, the download is reported done while the silent region is still hanging, and the second candidate is not asked before the hedge interval, or the hedge is a fan-out that doubles CDN load.
187.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db; config.json publishes edge-a (silent for audio) and edge-b (serving).

steps.action: Add a lecture while the preferred region never answers for audio.
steps.expected: It is added to the queue.

steps.action: Watch the download while the preferred region stays silent.
steps.expected: The other region is asked, serves the audio, and the lecture reaches the downloaded state.

steps.action: Check when the second candidate was first asked.
steps.expected: Not before the hedge interval — the head candidate ran alone first.

188.title: A rejected request refreshes once and is replayed
188.description: Offline. The access token is seeded an hour out so nothing proactive can fire; the server rejects the first authed call with 401 and accepts the replay. The answer must still arrive, the client must refresh exactly once, and the session must not drop to anonymous. Case 114 covers the proactive expiry-driven refresh; this covers the rejection the user actually hits when the device clock is off.
188.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db and a seeded signed-in session; /auth/refresh and /auth/me are mocked.

steps.action: Send a chat message while the server rejects the first authed call.
steps.expected: The answer arrives — the rejection is not terminal.

steps.action: Count the refreshes and the chat calls.
steps.expected: Exactly one refresh, and the rejected request was replayed once.

steps.action: Read the stored session.
steps.expected: Still signed in — no silent drop to anonymous.

190.title: A dead edge does not leave the device without an identity
190.description: Offline, with a two-region config. The app settles on edge-a, whose auth service returns 503. The anonymous mint is a device-keyed upsert against the one auth DB every region proxies to, so it must be re-issued on edge-b instead of stranding the device with no token at all (chat, sync and ingest off, and no probe that would notice — the startup probe only checks the storage host). Each door is asked exactly once, so the walk is a failover and not a fan-out at a failing backend.
190.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db and NO seeded session; config.json publishes edge-a (auth 503) and edge-b (minting).

steps.action: Launch the app with no stored session while the active region's auth service is down.
steps.expected: A token is minted anyway — the app is not left without an identity.

steps.action: Count the anonymous-mint calls per region.
steps.expected: The dead edge is asked once and the live one mints the identity once — a failover, not a fan-out.

191.title: A failed /me does not erase the signed-in profile
191.description: Offline, with a signed-in session about to expire. The next authed call refreshes the token, and the /me lookup that follows it returns 502. /me is best-effort — the client cannot tell a blip from a genuinely empty profile — so the account's email, name and avatar must be carried forward rather than written to null. They are persisted, so getting this wrong outlives the blip and the app restart: the signed-in user simply stops having a name until some later refresh happens to catch /me working.
191.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db; a stored non-anonymous session (name, email, avatar) whose access token expires within the refresh threshold; /auth/refresh succeeds and /auth/me returns 502.

steps.action: Send a chat message so the near-expiry token is refreshed, with /me failing.
steps.expected: The answer streams back — the refresh itself succeeded.

steps.action: Open Settings and look at the account row.
steps.expected: The account still shows the user's name, not a blank or anonymous row.

steps.action: Inspect the persisted session.
steps.expected: Email, name and avatar are still stored, so a restart does not inherit the blip.

192.title: The region follows the device without a cold start
192.description: Offline, with a two-region config. The app boots settled on edge-a. The device then relocates: edge-a stops answering and edge-b takes over, and the app is resumed and reports itself back online. The region must be re-detected there and then. Before this, probe() ran from exactly one place — the cold-start bootstrap — so a user who travelled, toggled a VPN or switched networks kept a stale region for as long as the process lived, which on mobile is days. That is the entry condition for the auth outage: API calls go to the wrong door, and the media layer's own walk corrupts and persists the region.
192.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db; config.json publishes edge-a and edge-b, both probing successfully at boot, with edge-a preferred.

steps.action: Launch the app and confirm the active region settled on edge-a.
steps.expected: edge-a is the persisted preferred region.

steps.action: Take edge-a offline, then resume the app and fire an online transition.
steps.expected: The app re-probes instead of waiting for the next cold start.

steps.action: Inspect the persisted preferred region.
steps.expected: It has moved to edge-b, so the next launch already starts on the right door.

193.title: A monologue reads as prose — no speaker-change marks
193.description: Offline. The fixture transcript is served with every sentence attributed to the same speaker. The reader breaks the text into paragraphs, and the grouper resets its running speaker at each break, so the speaker-change flag fires at the top of every paragraph. Gated only on that flag, a lecture by one person opened every paragraph with a stray dash. The dialogue affordances must be off entirely when there is one speaker.
193.preconditions: Offline fixtures, single-track user db; the transcript route serves a single-speaker transcript and the HTTP cache is cleared so the reader reads it.

steps.action: Open the transcript of a lecture whose transcript has one speaker.
steps.expected: The text renders with no speaker-change dash anywhere.

194.title: A dialogue keeps its speaker-change dash
194.description: Offline, the counterpart of case 191: the same fixture is served with the sentences alternating between two speakers. Hiding the dialogue affordances on a monologue must not hide them on an actual conversation — the dash is how a reader tells who is talking when the recording is a lecture plus questions from the floor.
194.preconditions: Offline fixtures, single-track user db; the transcript route serves a two-speaker transcript and the HTTP cache is cleared so the reader reads it.

steps.action: Open the transcript of a lecture whose transcript has two speakers.
steps.expected: The speaker-change dash renders.

steps.expected: "After 1 day" is the checked schedule.

steps.expected: The toggle is off and the live schedule reads "Never".

steps.action: Switch Smart Library back on.
steps.expected: "After 1 day" is checked again.

steps.expected: "Never" is still checked; "After 1 day" is not restored over it.

196.title: Smart Library topic filter survives a restart
196.description: Offline, Pro. A topic picked in the Smart Library filter sheet is persisted, not just shown: after a full reload the Filter row still summarises it and the sheet still shows it checked.

197.title: Audio owed an eviction is reclaimed, even across a relaunch
197.description: Offline, with a clean user db and two downloaded lectures. Archiving a lecture nothing is holding gives its space straight back — the control that proves the storage meter moves. Archiving the lecture that is PLAYING cannot: the engine holds a file:// URL, so the delete is deferred. That deferral used to live only in memory, so a relaunch lost it and nothing else in the app ever collected the orphan — the budget charged the user for that space until uninstall. The relaunch must settle the debt.
197.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db; the default 8 GB download limit.

steps.action: Add two lectures to the queue and let both download.
steps.expected: Both are queued and the storage figure in Settings accounts for them.

steps.action: Archive the first lecture, which nothing is playing.
steps.expected: Its row goes and the storage figure drops on the spot.

steps.action: Play the remaining lecture, then archive it while it plays.
steps.expected: Its row goes, but the storage figure holds — the file cannot be deleted while the engine holds it.

steps.action: Force-close and relaunch the app.
steps.expected: The launch reclaims the deferred file and the storage figure drops.

Guards the parser whitelist, which rebuilt each row as {tokens,title} so machine-translated canto titles shipped with no disclosure.

200.title: A lecture titled with ё is found by either spelling
200.description: SQLite folds Latin diacritics by itself but leaves Cyrillic `ё` as a term of its own, so this is the one spelling pair the app has to settle on both sides: lectorium-mcp folds the index (`008_fold_fts_marks`) and the query builder folds identically. The corpus spells the search word BOTH ways, so one query has to reach both titles — that is what makes the check sharp. Against a catalog predating the migration the query reaches only the `е`-spelled title however it is typed, and a bare "the two spellings agree" comparison would pass while half the corpus stayed unreachable (#1684). Offline, against the committed catalog fixture.
200.preconditions: Offline boot on a clean Russian user db, on the search tab. The catalog fixture carries one lecture titled "Душа остаётся загадкой для нас" and another titled "Душа всегда остается личностью", both within the seeded Bhagavad-gita source filter.

steps.action: Search a word spelled with ё ("остаётся").
steps.expected: Lectures are listed, and they include BOTH a title spelled with ё and one spelled with е.

steps.action: Search the same word spelled with е ("остается") — what a Russian keyboard actually produces.
steps.expected: Exactly the same lectures are listed.

The "My library" shelf on the Search landing leads to the full list, and the docked search field filters that list by title — down to its own "nothing found" state, which is NOT the empty-library state.

205.title: A subscriber adds a lecture found on the web and watches it through the pipeline
205.description: Offline, Pro, orchestrator stubbed. The plus on a web-lane hit submits the lecture's URL to the orchestrator, and the same tile then reports the run: an unnamed "Processing" the moment the submit returns, then the stages the status poll names — Downloading (with its ring) → Transcribing — and finally nothing at all, because a finished lecture is just a lecture. 206.title: A dead-lettered lecture is retried in place

An `add_to_library` action card is the chat's half of the personal library: chat is discovery-only, so confirming the candidate must submit through the orchestrator with the candidate's own URL and title, and the card must then show the same ingest badge the library tiles use.

steps.action: Tap the plus.
steps.expected: A submit reaches the orchestrator with the candidate's URL and title, and the card's corner turns into the ingest progress badge.

209.title: Sign in with an emailed code
209.description: Offline. The full email OTP journey from an anonymous app: Settings account row → provider sheet → email modal → request a code → enter it → land signed in. /auth/signin/email/request and /auth/signin/email/verify are mocked, and /auth/me answers as the anonymous user before the verify and as the reader's profile after it.
209.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db; the app booted as an anonymous user; the email OTP endpoints and /auth/me mocked.

steps.action: From Settings, tap the account row and choose "Continue with email".
steps.expected: The email sign-in modal opens on its first step, asking for an address.

steps.action: Enter an email address and tap "Send code".
steps.expected: The request is sent for that address and the form advances to the 6-digit code step.

steps.action: Enter the code and tap "Sign in".
steps.expected: The modal closes, the Settings account row shows the signed-in profile, and the persisted session is no longer anonymous.

210.title: Email sign-in upgrades the anonymous account in place
210.description: Offline. Everyone starts as an anonymous account that already owns their history, notes and chats. Signing in with an emailed code must claim THAT account rather than mint a second one — which works because the client attaches the anonymous access token as a Bearer to the verify call. The verify mock echoes the user id out of the bearer it is handed (and answers with a fresh id when handed none), so the assertion fails if the header goes missing.
210.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db; the app booted as an anonymous user; the email OTP endpoints and /auth/me mocked.

steps.action: Read the persisted session before signing in.
steps.expected: The app holds an anonymous session with a user id.

steps.action: Sign in with an emailed code (address, then code).
steps.expected: The modal completes and closes.

steps.action: Inspect the verify request and the persisted session.
steps.expected: The verify carried the anonymous bearer, and the stored session is the SAME user id — now non-anonymous and carrying the address.

211.title: A wrong or expired code is reported without losing the form
211.description: Offline. /auth/signin/email/verify answers 401 (invalid or expired code). The modal must show the reason inline and stay on the code step so the user can correct one digit, and no session may be granted.
211.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db; the app booted as an anonymous user; the code request succeeds and the verify is mocked to 401.

steps.action: From Settings, open the email sign-in modal and request a code.
steps.expected: The form advances to the code step.

steps.action: Enter a code the server rejects.
steps.expected: The modal shows "That code is invalid or has expired." inline.

steps.action: Check what the user is left with.
steps.expected: Still on the code step with the submit button live, and the session is still anonymous — nothing was granted.

212.title: A throttled code request is reported, not swallowed
212.description: Offline. /auth/signin/email/request answers 429 with Retry-After (a code was just sent, or the per-IP budget burst). The modal must surface the throttle and stay on the email step — advancing to a code step for a code that was never sent would leave the user waiting for mail that is not coming.
212.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db; the app booted as an anonymous user; the code request is mocked to 429.

steps.action: From Settings, open the email sign-in modal, enter an address and tap "Send code" while the server throttles.
steps.expected: The modal shows "Please wait a moment before requesting another code." inline.

steps.action: Check what the user is left with.
steps.expected: Still on the email step: the address is still in the field, "Send code" is live again, and no verify was attempted.

213.title: A backend outage does not sign the user out
213.description: Offline. A signed-in session whose access token sits inside the 60s refresh window runs while /auth/refresh answers 503 — the shape of an auth deploy or DB blip. A refresh failure has three outcomes, not two: only a 401/403 rejection may drop the session; a transient failure must keep it so a later attempt recovers. What is asserted is not that the session looks intact right after the 503 (that read races the client's own handling and passes either way) but that the next authed call recovers by REFRESHING the same session, with no anonymous identity minted along the way — a client that mistook the outage for a rejection would have thrown the account away, bootstrapped a stranger, and answered the chat just the same. Cases 114 and 188 only ever see the refresh succeed, so this branch was never executed by a test.
213.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db; a signed-in session seeded with an access token expiring in ~30s; /auth/refresh, /auth/anonymous, /auth/me and the chat stream mocked.

steps.action: Boot the signed-in session while auth refuses every refresh with 503.
steps.expected: At least one refresh is attempted and refused.

steps.action: Bring auth back, then send a chat message — an authed call that needs a token.
steps.expected: The answer streams back, and the token came from a further REFRESH of the same session: no new anonymous account was minted.

steps.action: Inspect the persisted session and open Settings.
steps.expected: Still non-anonymous, and the account row still shows the signed-in profile rather than the anonymous “Sign in” call to action.

214.title: A topic shelf folds playback progress like the shelves beside it
214.description: The Search landing is a discovery surface end to end, but its personalized topic shelves built their rows without saying so — so a lecture being played showed a progress radial there while "Recommended for you" a few sections up showed the flat added/completed badge for the same track (#1615). Offline, on the seeded English profile whose listening history is what produces the shelves at all.
214.preconditions: Offline boot (mocked content + silent mp3) on the seeded English user db, so the landing derives topic shelves from listening history. A shelf lecture is not yet in the queue — discovery never resurfaces a queued or completed one.

steps.action: On the Search tab, add the first lecture of a topic shelf to the queue, then play it from the Home queue.
steps.expected: The player opens on that lecture.

steps.action: Return to the Search tab and look at the same lecture's row in its topic shelf.
steps.expected: The row shows the flat added/completed state badge — the same one the other shelves show — not a progress radial.

220.title: A user database that cannot be opened shows an error screen, not an onboarding loop
220.description: Offline. Seeds a corrupt user.db so opening it fails while the catalog opens fine, and asserts the app lands on a terminal storage-error screen that names the failure — instead of bouncing every route to onboarding, whose Finish navigates straight back into the guard.
220.preconditions: Seeded offline fixtures. The user database in IndexedDB is replaced with bytes that are not a SQLite file; no onboarding.completed flag is set.

steps.action: Launch the app with a user database that cannot be opened.
steps.expected: The storage-error screen is shown with the underlying failure quoted; onboarding is not shown.

steps.action: Navigate directly to a tab route (deep link to Home).
steps.expected: The app stays on the storage-error screen and never redirects to onboarding.

steps.action: Tap "Try again" while the database is still unreadable.
steps.expected: The app reloads and returns to the same error screen — no blank screen and no loop.

221.title: Startup still signs the device in when the user database fails to open
221.description: Offline. The listening-history probe used to throw synchronously past its catch and abort the rest of startup, leaving the run with no session and every authenticated call returning 401. Asserts the anonymous sign-in still happens when the user database is unreadable.
221.preconditions: Seeded offline fixtures. The user database in IndexedDB is replaced with bytes that are not a SQLite file. POST /auth/anonymous is mocked and recorded.

steps.action: Launch the app with a user database that cannot be opened, recording POST /auth/anonymous.
steps.expected: The storage-error screen is shown.

steps.action: Wait for the anonymous session request.
steps.expected: The app minted a session — startup continued past the failed database probe.

225.title: The chat's add-to-library card survives a paywall bounce
225.description: Offline, FREE tier, orchestrator stubbed. Adding a lecture is Pro, so a non-subscriber tapping the chat candidate's plus is bounced to the subscription page and nothing is submitted — the designed path for every free user. The card must therefore still be an offer when they come back: it used to record the tap as done, drop its plus, and persist that, leaving an inert tile over a lecture nobody ever fetched (#1727).
225.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db, booted as a FREE user; the chat SSE stream is mocked with an add_to_library action and its marker, and the orchestrator ingest API is stubbed so a submit would be recorded if one happened.

steps.action: Ask the chat a question whose mocked answer carries an add-to-library candidate.
steps.expected: The answer renders the candidate as a tile with its title and a plus.

steps.action: Tap the plus as a free user.
steps.expected: The subscription page opens and no submit reaches the orchestrator.

steps.action: Dismiss the subscription page and return to the conversation.
steps.expected: The candidate tile still offers its plus, so the lecture can be added after subscribing.

235.title: A saved bookmark underlines only the sentence it was taken on
235.description: Offline. Sentence blocks in this corpus are commonly contiguous (end_i === start_{i+1}), and the saved-note pass treated a shared endpoint as an overlap, so a one-sentence bookmark painted the wavy underline across its neighbours and bled the note id onto them (#1731). Long-presses inside ONE sentence, bookmarks it, and asserts exactly one underlined span, on that sentence's own time range.
235.preconditions: Offline boot (mocked content + silent mp3) on the single-track user.db, which carries no seeded notes. A queued track can be played and its transcript opened.

steps.action: Open a queued track's transcript, long-press and drag inside a single sentence, then tap the bookmark action in the selection popover.
steps.expected: The note is saved and the selection popover closes.

steps.action: Inspect the wavy underlines painted over the transcript.
steps.expected: Exactly one span is underlined, and its time range is the selected sentence's own.

236.title: A transcript drag saves exactly the span it highlighted
236.description: Offline. While dragging, each branch emitted a range built from the fixed anchor while the release emitted the running pair, so a drag that crossed the anchor one way and back the other collapsed the highlight while the far edge stayed extended - the saved note, the Ask Sadhu text and the share payload then covered a span the user never saw selected (#1732). Drags past the anchor in both directions, reads the live highlight before releasing, and compares it with the underline the saved note paints.
236.preconditions: Offline boot (mocked content + silent mp3) on the single-track user.db, which carries no seeded notes. The open transcript shows at least three sentences on screen.

steps.action: In an open transcript, long-press a sentence, drag past its end, drag back past its start, note the highlighted span, release and tap the bookmark action.
steps.expected: The selection popover opens on release and the note is saved.

steps.action: Compare the underline painted by the saved note with the highlight shown at the moment of release.
steps.expected: They cover exactly the same sentences.

240.title: Email sign-in refreshes a stale token before claiming the anonymous account
240.description: Offline. Days without a network leave the stored access token expired but present — the adapter keeps the session on a network error rather than signing the user out. The sign-in call must therefore rotate the token before attaching it: an expired bearer fails server-side verification, so the server skips the in-place upgrade and creates a brand-new account, orphaning the anonymous user's library (#1737). The verify mock rejects an expired bearer the way the real verifier does.
240.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db; a persisted ANONYMOUS session whose access token expired an hour ago; /auth/refresh answers 503 (transient — the adapter keeps the session) until the code is submitted, so the token is still stale when sign-in begins; /auth/me and the email OTP endpoints mocked.

steps.action: Read the persisted session before signing in.
steps.expected: The app holds the anonymous account, on an access token that has already expired.

steps.action: Sign in with an emailed code (address, then code).
steps.expected: The modal completes and closes.

steps.action: Inspect the token rotation and the bearer the verify carried.
steps.expected: The client refreshed the stale token first, and the bearer it sent has an expiry in the future.

steps.action: Read the persisted session after signing in.
steps.expected: It is the SAME user id, now non-anonymous — the anonymous account was upgraded, not orphaned.

270.title: A stalled chat stream recovers the answer from the resume poll
270.description: Offline. A HALF-OPEN stream — the server accepts the turn, writes a status frame and a delta, then goes quiet without closing — is the failure the 45 s stall timeout (#1547) exists for, and it cannot be expressed as a route mock: a fulfilled route delivers the whole body at once, so it is never mid-stream and never hanging. A real Node socket (support/sse-server.ts) is reached by pointing a region's chatBaseUrl at it via a config.json fixture. GET /chat/turn/* answers with the finished turn, so the stall must end in the buffered answer being replayed — with no failure surfaced to the user.
270.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db and mocked auth. A one-region config whose chatBaseUrl points at a local SSE server that writes `status` + one `delta` and then stalls forever; GET /chat/turn/* mocked with a `done` turn carrying the full answer.

steps.action: Send a question to a chat endpoint that streams one status frame and one partial delta, then goes silent.
steps.expected: The partial prose renders and the thinking pill shows the server's own status label.

steps.action: Wait out the stall timeout without any further bytes on the socket.
steps.expected: The resume poll is made and the full buffered answer replaces the partial text.

steps.action: Inspect the conversation once the answer has landed.
steps.expected: No failed bubble and no inline notice — the recovered stall is invisible to the user, and the thinking pill is gone.

271.title: A stalled turn the server cannot account for offers a Retry
271.description: Offline. The other outcome of a stall (#1677): the socket goes half-open before any prose and the server has no buffered turn, so every resume poll 404s. Recovery is attempted and comes back empty, and once the recovery window closes the thinking placeholder becomes the SAME inline notice + Retry the failed bubble uses (case 83) rather than spinning until the 24 h buffer TTL. Tapping Retry re-sends the question — a second POST /chat on the wire.
271.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db and mocked auth. A one-region config whose chatBaseUrl points at a local SSE server that sends headers and then nothing at all; GET /chat/turn/* answers 404 on every poll.

steps.action: Send a question to a chat endpoint that answers with headers and then goes silent.
steps.expected: The question echoes into the thread and the answer shows as still generating.

steps.action: Wait out the stall timeout and the resume-recovery window, with every turn poll answering 404.
steps.expected: The placeholder becomes an inline notice carrying a Retry button.

steps.action: Tap Retry.
steps.expected: The same question is re-sent — a second POST /chat reaches the server.

283.title: A conversation at the server's 20-message cap accepts the next question
283.description: Offline. ChatRequestDto.messages is max_length=20 and pydantic REJECTS a longer list rather than truncating it, so a client replaying its full local history got a 422 on the 21st message — and 422 is not a transient status, so the turn failed and Retry re-sent the same oversized body. The conversation was unsendable for good (#1771). The regression is in the REQUEST, not in the rendering, so the spec builds a real 20-message session through the UI over ten mocked turns and then inspects the wire payload of the eleventh.
283.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db and mocked chat auth. POST /chat is intercepted by a mock that records each request body and answers with a numbered SSE answer.

steps.action: Ask ten questions in a row, waiting for each streamed answer, so the session holds twenty messages.
steps.expected: Every turn is answered and the tenth request carries nineteen turns — still under the server's cap.

steps.action: Ask an eleventh question from the same session, which is now at the cap.
steps.expected: The turn is answered normally — no error bubble, no failed send.

steps.action: Inspect the request body of that eleventh send.
steps.expected: It carries exactly twenty turns, ending with the question just asked; the opening exchange has been dropped from the window.

286.title: Signing out wipes the account's data from the device
286.description: Offline. A signed-in account signs out; the local user data (notes, playlist, listening history, chat) is wiped silently — no confirmation dialog — while the public lecture catalog is spared, and a toast tells the user the data stays in the account and comes back on the next sign-in while the downloaded lectures are gone and must be re-fetched. An unclaimed anonymous session is deliberately exempt (it has nothing to restore from), which this case does not cover.
286.preconditions: Signed in via preseeded auth tokens (profile "E2E Tester"); seeded user DB with notes; app booted offline with /auth/signout mocked.

steps.action: Open the Notes tab.
steps.expected: The account's seeded notes are listed.

steps.action: Open Settings, tap the account row and choose Sign out.
steps.expected: No confirmation is asked; a toast says the data stays in the account and returns on the next sign-in, and that the downloaded lectures were deleted from this device.

steps.action: Reopen the Notes tab.
steps.expected: No notes remain on the device, and searching the library still lists lectures (the public catalog was not dropped).

298.title: Notes search with no match shows a 'nothing found' state
298.description: Offline. Types a string no seeded note contains into the Notes search box and asserts the page renders a 'nothing found' sticker instead of a blank list, then that clearing the box brings the notes back.
298.preconditions: Seeded offline fixture with one or more notes on the Notes tab.

steps.action: Open the Notes tab and type a string that matches none of the notes into the search box.
steps.expected: The list empties and a sticker with a 'Nothing found' heading and an explanatory message renders in its place — the page is never blank.

steps.action: Clear the search box.
steps.expected: The sticker disappears and the full notes list is restored.

301.title: A rejected add of a web lecture tells the user it failed
301.description: Offline. `addByUrl` reports its outcome, but the plus on a web result used to throw that report away, and a rejected submit records no job id — so the tile keeps its plus, no badge appears, and the only haptic already fired before the request left. The tap was indistinguishable from a dead button whenever the orchestrator was down (#1778). The submit failure now speaks in a toast, and the tile stays an offer so the lecture can be added again once the service is back.
301.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db, booted as a subscriber so the client-side Pro gate passes; the ingest mock rejects POST /orchestrator/run with 503 internal.

steps.action: Open the library and tap the plus on the first lecture in the internet lane, with the ingest service rejecting every submit.
steps.expected: A toast reports that the lecture could not be added, and the request did reach the orchestrator.

steps.action: Inspect the tile once the failure has been reported.
steps.expected: It is still an offer — the plus is there and no ingest badge appeared — so the lecture can be added again.

steps.action: Dismiss the toast and tap the plus a second time, with the service still rejecting.
steps.expected: The failure is reported again and a second submit reaches the orchestrator — the first rejection is not sticky.

304.title: Signing in from the quota banner re-sends the question exactly once
304.description: The anonymous conversion funnel. A 429 on the anonymous tier locks the composer and shows the sign-in upsell; taking that CTA and completing email sign-in flips quota_id and signedIn in one session apply, which used to fire the quota re-send twice in the same Vue flush and leave the question on screen twice with the dead limit card between them (#1779). Offline - auth and /chat both mocked; /chat answers 429 on the anonymous ask and streams a real answer to the re-send.
304.preconditions: Chat reachable offline; mocked anonymous auth; email OTP request/verify mocked so verify returns the same user id, non-anonymous, with a new quota_id claim; /chat mocked to 429 (tier anonymous) on the first ask and to stream an answer afterwards.

steps.action: Ask a question as an anonymous user and hit the daily limit (429).
steps.expected: The composer is disabled and the upsell notice offers a "Sign in" action.

steps.action: Tap the notice's sign-in action and complete email sign-in (address, then code).
steps.expected: The sign-in modal closes and the session is upgraded in place.

steps.action: Inspect the conversation after the sign-in.
steps.expected: The question was re-sent and answered, it appears exactly once, and the quota notice is gone.

307.title: Quota lock survives the suggestion pills
307.description: Offline. With the daily chat quota exhausted, the empty-state suggestion pills render disabled and tapping one — including a click dispatched straight at the handler, which a disabled button does not suppress — issues no /chat request and starts no session. Auth mocked as free; /chat mocked to return a free-tier 429 for every call, so a second request is visible as a count.
307.preconditions: Chat reachable offline; mocked auth (free tier); /chat mocked to answer every request with a 429 free-tier quota body (current=limit=5, reset an hour out).

steps.action: Send a question that hits the free quota limit (429).
steps.expected: The composer textarea is disabled and exactly one request reached /chat.

steps.action: Tap "New chat" in the header to return to the empty state.
steps.expected: The suggestion pills are shown, rendered disabled, and the composer stays locked.

steps.action: Tap a suggestion pill, then dispatch its click programmatically to bypass the disabled attribute.
steps.expected: No further /chat request is issued, no conversation is started, and the composer stays locked.

319.title: Deleting a conversation with an unread reply clears the Sadhu tab dot
319.description: Offline, mocked SSE with a delayed answer. A reply lands while the user is away from the conversation, lighting the Sadhu tab's unread dot; the conversation is then deleted from history without ever being opened. Regression for #1784, where the dot stayed lit forever with no session left to open.
319.preconditions: Clean offline user fixture (no seeded chat history). The chat backend is mocked and the answer is held back, so the turn is still running when the user leaves the conversation.

steps.action: On the chat tab, send a question, then tap New chat and switch to the Home tab before the answer arrives.
steps.expected: Home is shown and the conversation is left unopened.

steps.action: Wait for the answer to arrive in the background.
steps.expected: The Sadhu tab shows the unread dot.

steps.action: Return to the chat tab (the empty state, not the conversation) and open the history sheet.
steps.expected: The conversation holding the unread reply is listed.

steps.action: Swipe that conversation open and delete it, then re-open history.
steps.expected: The conversation is gone and the Sadhu tab's unread dot is cleared, including after the sessions list reloads.

332.title: Only the search page on top asks the archives — one request per pause
332.description: The docked search field is shared by the library tab and the pages it pushes on top of it, and the tab stays mounted underneath them. Typing on the full-results page must therefore issue exactly ONE search request — the page that is showing — not one from every page that has ever read the field. Offline, with the search service stubbed and its requests counted.
332.preconditions: Offline boot on a clean user db. The discovery search endpoint is stubbed and every request body is recorded.

steps.action: Search the library tab, then tap the chevron on the "found on the internet" shelf.
steps.expected: The full set opens on its own page and lists its tiles.

steps.action: With the arrival's own search settled and the counter cleared, type new words into the docked field and wait out both typing debounces.
steps.expected: Exactly one search request was sent, and no further one arrives.

333.title: The library tab searches the words typed on the page above it
333.description: The field is shared, so it can be edited from a page pushed on top of the library tab. The tab does not search while it is covered; going back to it must therefore re-run the query for whatever the field now holds, rather than leaving the results of the previous words on screen. Offline.
333.preconditions: Offline boot on a clean user db, with library results on screen for a broad query.

steps.action: Open the full internet-results page from the shelf's chevron and replace the query in the docked field with one the catalog cannot match.
steps.expected: The page above stays on screen with the field holding the new words.

steps.action: Go back to the library tab.
steps.expected: The library lane shows its "nothing matches" empty state — the rows for the previous query are gone.

334.title: A collection that cannot be loaded says so
334.description: Component test (vitest, not Playwright — a missing collection is not reachable from the mocked fixture, whose collections all exist in both languages). A collection the catalog does not hold in the current content language, and one whose read throws, each render their own PageSticker instead of the title-less, message-less page that was pixel-identical to an empty collection. 244 of 265 collection ids exist in one language only, so switching the content language with the page open is the everyday way in.
334.preconditions: The collection detail page mounted with a repository that returns null for the requested id, or throws.

steps.action: Open a collection the catalog does not hold in the current content language.
steps.expected: The page shows the 'collection unavailable' header and the message naming the library language, no track list, and no empty hero.

steps.action: Open a collection whose read throws.
steps.expected: The page shows the 'could not load' message and no track list.

steps.action: Open a collection that loads but holds no lectures.
steps.expected: No error message: the hero carries the collection title and the (empty) track list renders.

335.title: An empty track list renders nothing, not a blank row
335.description: Component test (vitest, not Playwright). TracksList used to render a full-height IonItem whenever it had no rows, carrying an emptyMessage that defaults to the empty string — a blank grey row that reads as content. No caller passes a message today, so the row is now suppressed unless there is something to say; the message row itself still works for a caller that supplies one.
335.preconditions: None — the list component is rendered directly.

steps.action: Render the track list with no rows and no empty message.
steps.expected: Nothing is rendered: no row, no text.

steps.action: Render the track list with no rows and an empty message.
steps.expected: A single row carrying that message.

steps.action: Render the track list with rows.
steps.expected: The rows render and no empty row is added.

336.title: An added internet result opens on the same sheet as the library tile
336.description: Offline, Pro, orchestrator stubbed. A lecture the user already added is still shown by the internet lane, and its tile now stands for the lecture itself: the corner stops offering a plus and the tile announces itself as a button. Tapping it resolves the hit back to its personal-library row (matched by source URL) and presents the same track sheet the “My library” tile presents — including the “Remove from My library” action, which only a resolved library item has.
336.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db, booted as a subscriber; the ingest mock seeds one READY library item whose source URL is the first internet-lane hit and which carries a track id.

steps.action: Search the library and wait for the internet shelf, with the seeded lecture already in the personal library.
steps.expected: The first tile no longer offers a plus and carries role="button".

steps.action: Tap that tile.
steps.expected: The track sheet opens, titled with the lecture, and offers the remove-from-library action.

337.title: An internet result with nothing to open is not a button
337.description: Offline, Pro, orchestrator stubbed. The counterpart of case 336: a tile may only claim to be a button when there is a lecture behind it. A hit still being fetched reports its stage and is not tappable; a hit whose library row is ready but resolves to no track is not tappable either, and tapping it opens nothing rather than swallowing the tap (#1788).
337.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db, booted as a subscriber; the ingest mock seeds one item still processing (first hit) and one ready item with no track id (second hit).

steps.action: Search the library and read the tile of the lecture that is still being fetched.
steps.expected: The corner reports the stage and the tile carries no button role.

steps.action: Read the tile whose library row is ready but has no track, then tap it.
steps.expected: The tile offers no plus, carries no button role, and the tap opens no track sheet.

349.title: A server error mid-answer is not reported as a dropped connection
349.description: Offline. The mocked SSE stream writes one prose delta and then a terminal `error` frame with code `turn_timeout` — the socket is fine, the agent gave up. The bubble must keep the partial prose and carry the generic "could not be completed" suffix instead of the "connection dropped" copy that is reserved for a real transport drop (#1795).
349.preconditions: Chat reachable offline (mocked auth); POST /chat is mocked as an SSE stream of one delta followed by an `error` frame with code `turn_timeout`.

steps.action: Send a question whose stream emits one prose delta and then a `turn_timeout` error frame.
steps.expected: The partial answer text stays on screen in the assistant bubble.

steps.action: Read the truncation label appended to the assistant bubble.
steps.expected: It says the answer could not be completed, and does NOT say the connection dropped.

352.title: Turning off "Sync chats" stops conversations arriving from other devices
352.description: Offline. The mocked `POST /profile/sync/pull` serves an append-only change log holding one conversation started on another device. With "Sync chats" off the device must not apply it in either direction; turning the setting back on rewinds the pull cursor to where the skipping began, so the conversation is recovered rather than lost for good (#1848).
352.preconditions: Clean user DB seeded once (so the pull cursor survives the relaunch). `POST /profile/sync/pull` is mocked as a cursor-respecting change log, initially empty.

steps.action: Open Settings and turn "Sync chats" off, then publish a conversation from another device to the change log and relaunch the app so a full sync cycle runs.
steps.expected: The setting reads off and the app completes at least one pull cycle after the conversation was published.

steps.action: Open the chat history sheet.
steps.expected: The conversation from the other device is not listed and the history is empty.

steps.action: Turn "Sync chats" back on and re-open the chat history sheet.
steps.expected: The conversation that was skipped while the setting was off now appears in the history.

353.title: Retry stays disabled while the daily limit is armed
353.description: Offline. Retrying a turn drops the question and its reply before re-sending, and a send while the quota lock is armed returns immediately — so an enabled Retry there erases the question from every device and starts nothing (#1837). The control must read as unavailable and change nothing when tapped.
353.preconditions: Chat reachable offline (mocked auth, free tier). POST /chat answers the first turn with an SSE stream that streams prose and then a `turn_timeout` error frame, and every later turn with a 429 carrying a free-tier quota body.

steps.action: Ask a question whose stream dies mid-prose, and look at the assistant bubble's actions row.
steps.expected: The partial answer is kept and its Retry control is enabled.

steps.action: Start a new chat and ask another question, which the server rejects with a free-tier 429.
steps.expected: The composer is locked and the limit notice is shown.

steps.action: Reopen the earlier conversation from the history sheet, so its truncated answer is the last bubble again, and tap its Retry.
steps.expected: Retry is visible but disabled; the question and its partial answer are still there and no new request went out.

354.title: A buffered answer survives asking a new question mid-recovery
354.description: Offline, real socket. A turn whose stream stalls is followed by a resume poll; asking a new question while that poll runs used to make it abandon the turn without one last look at the server, discarding an answer that was already generated and buffered (#1840). The recovered answer must still land, above the newer question.
354.preconditions: Chat points at the local stalling SSE server; GET /chat/turn/<id> reports the followed turn `running` until the new question has been sent, then `done` with its buffered events.

steps.action: Ask a question on a socket that writes one prose frame and then goes quiet, and wait for the stall to hand the turn to the resume poll.
steps.expected: The partial prose is on screen and the turn is being polled for.

steps.action: Ask a second question while the resume poll is still running, then let the server report the first turn done.
steps.expected: The buffered answer to the first question appears.

steps.action: Read the order of the thread.
steps.expected: The recovered answer sits above the second question, not after it.

381.title: A hung token refresh does not wedge the session
381.description: A /auth/refresh that opens a socket and never answers (a hang, NOT a rejection — plain offline rejects immediately and never reproduced this) must not strand every later authed call on the same memoised promise. Seeds a near-expiry session, hangs /auth/refresh, sends a chat message, then lets the service answer and retries. Offline — mocked auth + SSE.
381.preconditions: Signed-in session seeded with an access token expiring in ~30s; /auth/refresh hangs without answering; /auth/me and the chat stream mocked.

steps.action: Open Chat and send a message while /auth/refresh hangs without answering.
steps.expected: The hung refresh is bounded and released: the client issues a SECOND /auth/refresh rather than leaving every later authed call joined to one dead memoised promise.

steps.action: Wait for the send to come back with a Retry notice, let /auth/refresh answer again, and tap Retry.
steps.expected: A fresh token is minted and persisted (the stored expiry moves an hour out) — the session recovered on its own, with no force-quit.

361.title: A failed add says which failure it was
361.description: Offline. Every rejected add to the personal library used to read "check your connection and try again" — including a missing token, our own 15 s timeout and any orchestrator 4xx/5xx (#1844). The reason now travels out of the store with the failure, so a backend that answered badly and a request that never left the device produce two different sentences.
361.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db, booted as a subscriber so the client-side Pro gate passes. The ingest mock is installed; the spec varies only how POST /orchestrator/run fails.

steps.action: With the orchestrator answering 503, tap the plus on the first lecture in the internet lane.
steps.expected: The toast blames the service, not the connection.

steps.action: Dismiss the toast, then make the submit fail before it reaches a server and tap the plus again.
steps.expected: The toast now names the connection — the two causes do not share a sentence.

420.title: Note cards show the lecture date localized, not as a raw ISO string
420.description: Offline. Every other lecture surface localizes the recording date; the note card printed the raw `YYYY-MM-DD` it got from the catalog. Asserts no note's meta line carries an ISO date and that any date it does carry reads in the locale's form.
420.preconditions: Seeded offline fixture with notes on lectures that carry a recording date. App locale: en.

steps.action: Open the Notes tab and wait for the notes to render.
steps.expected: At least one note is listed.

steps.action: Read the attribution line of every note card.
steps.expected: No line contains a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, and every date shown reads as `D Mon YYYY`.

440.title: Smart Library filters are shared between Settings and the Library
440.description: Offline, Pro. Both screens hold their own binding over one persisted filter set and both stay mounted for the app's lifetime. A dimension set on one screen must be visible on the other, and editing a different dimension there must not erase it.
440.preconditions: Offline fixtures with a clean user db, booted as a subscriber. Both the Library tab and the Settings tab are visited so both bindings are alive.

steps.action: Visit the Library tab, then open Settings and pick a topic in the Smart Library filter sheet.
steps.expected: The Settings Filter row summarises the chosen topic.

steps.action: Return to the Library tab and open its Smart Library dialog.
steps.expected: The Library Filter row summarises the same topic, not "All lectures".

steps.action: From the Library sheet pick an author, then reopen the Smart Library dialog in Settings.
steps.expected: The Filter row lists both the author and the topic — the topic was not overwritten by the Library screen's edit.

350.title: A corrupt user database can be reset from the storage-error screen
350.description: Device-only. A `user.db` that deterministically fails to open parks the app on /storage-error, whose retry re-runs the same failing bootstrap and whose Settings are behind the router guard. The screen must offer a destructive reset that deletes the user-database file WITHOUT going through repositories(), and must spare the downloaded lecture catalog so recovery does not cost a ~54 MB re-download (#1831).
350.preconditions: A build with the storage reset. Root/file access to the app sandbox, or a device where the user database can be replaced with garbage (e.g. import a non-SQLite file, or overwrite <name>SQLite.db).

steps.action: Corrupt the user database on the device (overwrite it with non-SQLite bytes) and cold-start the app.
steps.expected: The app opens on the storage-error screen and prints the underlying failure message.

steps.action: Tap the retry action.
steps.expected: The app reloads and lands back on the storage-error screen — retry alone cannot recover.

steps.action: Tap the destructive reset action and dismiss the confirm dialog without confirming.
steps.expected: Nothing is deleted and the screen is unchanged.

steps.action: Tap the reset action again and confirm.
steps.expected: The app reloads, bootstraps into a fresh empty user database, and reaches Home or onboarding — no reinstall needed.

steps.action: Open the app's storage and check the catalog file under the databases directory, then open Search.
steps.expected: The downloaded lecture catalog is still on disk and search returns results with no foreground download.

351.title: The bundled catalog is not re-copied on every cold start
351.description: Device-only, Android first (the asset is DEFLATE-compressed in the APK, so the copy is a full inflate on the main thread before the first frame). Once a newer catalog has been downloaded, the JS prune deletes the bundled file and the native helper must NOT put it back; it must copy again only when an app update ships a catalog newer than the one on disk, or when the on-disk file fails the SQLite header gate (#1830).
351.preconditions: A device with the app installed and a catalog newer than the bundled one already downloaded (launch once, let the background refresh finish, relaunch).

steps.action: List the app's lectorium/databases directory and note which lectorium.<version>.db files are present.
steps.expected: Only the downloaded catalog is present; the bundled version has been pruned.

steps.action: Cold-start the app and watch the BundledDatabaseHelper log line.
steps.expected: It logs a skip, not a copy, and the bundled file does not reappear in the directory.

steps.action: Time the cold start against the previous build.
steps.expected: No multi-second stall before the first frame.

steps.action: Truncate the on-disk catalog to a few non-SQLite bytes and cold-start again.
steps.expected: The helper copies the bundled catalog back — the corrupt file must not win the version comparison.

steps.action: Install a build whose bundled catalog is NEWER than the one on disk and cold-start.
steps.expected: The bundled catalog is copied, and the JS prune then removes the older downloaded one.

500.title: A failed internet search is asked again when the page comes back
500.description: Offline. The lane remembers the words it last asked the archives for, so returning to the page does not re-buy an answer already on the shelf. A search that FAILED answered nothing, so those words must not count as answered: with the service reachable again, leaving the search tab and returning re-asks and the shelf fills. The lane has no retry button, so this is the only gesture that can (#1842).
500.preconditions: Offline boot on a clean user db. The discovery search endpoint is stubbed and answers 503 for the first search.

steps.action: Search the library tab while the internet search service answers 503.
steps.expected: The "found on the internet" shelf shows its unreachable-service strip.

steps.action: With the service answering normally again, leave the search tab and come back to it without touching the field.
steps.expected: The shelf re-asks and lists its tiles; the unreachable-service strip is gone.

460.title: Quota lock reaches the outline card's chapter rows
460.description: Offline. With the daily chat quota exhausted, the chapter rows of an outline card already in the thread render disabled and dimmed, and tapping one — including a click dispatched straight at the handler, which a disabled button does not suppress — issues no /chat request. Auth mocked as free; /chat answers the first turn with an SSE outline card and every later turn with a free-tier 429, so a further request is visible as a count.
460.preconditions: Chat reachable offline; mocked auth (free tier); /chat mocked to stream an outline action + marker on the first call and a 429 free-tier quota body (current=limit=5, reset an hour out) on every call after it.

steps.action: Ask a question whose answer carries an outline card.
steps.expected: The outline card renders its chapter rows, the rows are enabled and the composer is usable.

steps.action: Send a second question, which the server refuses with a free-tier 429.
steps.expected: The limit notice appears, the composer is disabled, and the chapter rows of the earlier answer are disabled too. Exactly two requests reached /chat.

steps.action: Tap a chapter row, then dispatch its click programmatically to bypass the disabled attribute.
steps.expected: No further /chat request is made and the composer stays locked.

520.title: Signing out with chat sync off says the conversations were deleted
520.description: Offline. Journaling is gated by the device-local "Sync chats" toggle, so with it off the account never holds a copy of the conversations — and sign-out wipes the device's only one. The toast is the user's only notice (there is deliberately no confirmation dialog), so it must say the chats were deleted and name the downloads instead of promising everything comes back on the next sign-in.
520.preconditions: Signed in via preseeded auth tokens (profile "E2E Tester"); app booted offline with /auth/signout mocked.

steps.action: Open Settings and turn "Sync chats" off.
steps.expected: The toggle reads off.

steps.action: Tap the account row and choose Sign out.
steps.expected: A toast says the conversations were deleted and that the downloaded lectures were removed from this device; it does NOT claim the chats stay in the account.

540.title: Composer empties after sending and a second Enter sends nothing
540.description: Offline (mocked auth + mocked SSE stream). Asserts the chat composer is blank once the question is away, and that pressing Enter again on the emptied capsule does not fire a second chat turn — the duplicate, quota-counted turn of #1885.
540.preconditions: Chat reachable. Mocked anonymous auth and a mocked SSE stream of one answer delta + done.

steps.action: Type a question in the chat composer and send it.
steps.expected: The question echoes into the thread as a user bubble and the composer is empty.

steps.action: Wait for the answer to stream, then press Enter in the empty composer.
steps.expected: No second chat request is made and the question still appears exactly once.

550.title: Leaving the Studio mid-render lights the background-share indicator
550.description: Offline, Pro-booted. The video renderer accepts the job but the file never lands, so the render is still running when the user walks away. Asserts that leaving the Studio moves the job to the background: the Notes tab shows the share spinner, which is the only thing that explains the "Another share is already in progress" refusal every other share surface gives out for as long as the render holds the app-wide slot (#1886).
550.preconditions: Seeded offline fixture with notes, booted as Pro. The share-video endpoint accepts the render request; the rendered MP4 never becomes available.

steps.action: Open a note's Share menu and tap Share video to open the Studio.
steps.expected: The Studio editor opens with the note's text.

steps.action: Tap Download and stay on the page.
steps.expected: The render starts and the Notes tab still shows its normal icon — the user can see the progress right where they are.

steps.action: Leave the Studio for the Notes tab while the render is still running.
steps.expected: The Notes tab icon is replaced by the background-share spinner, so the held share slot has a visible cause.

551.title: Share audio hands off to the background instead of pinning the app
551.description: Offline. The lecture's audio request never answers — the parked-transfer shape. Asserts the share modal, which has neither a backdrop dismiss nor a cancel, gives the UI back after the 3-second handoff instead of holding it: the modal closes, the user is told the share continues in the background, and the Notes tab spinner shows the app-wide share slot is still held (#1889).
551.preconditions: Seeded offline fixture (clean user DB) with a library track that has audio. The audio URL hangs without ever answering.

steps.action: Open a library track's sheet, tap Share, then tap Audio.
steps.expected: The prepare spinner is presented over the app while the download starts.

steps.action: Wait out the handoff without touching anything.
steps.expected: The modal closes on its own, a toast says the share continues in the background, and the Notes tab shows the background-share spinner.

590.title: Onboarding seeds Home with the lectures it showed
590.description: Offline. The value-moment screen lists the lectures matched to the picked topic; Home must open on exactly those, not on a second draw from the same topic pool (issue #1888). Picks the second curated topic, the one whose fixture pool is larger than the five shown.
590.preconditions: Fresh first launch: onboarding.completed unset and a clean user DB with NO listening history and an empty playlist. Non-Pro subscription state. Content is served from offline intercepts.

steps.action: Launch the app, advance past Welcome, pick the second topic chip, and continue to the Daily wisdom slide, choosing a time preset.
steps.expected: Each tap advances one slide; leaving the topics slide confirms the picks.

steps.action: Continue to the Value moment slide and record the lecture titles it lists once the list settles.
steps.expected: The screen lists more than one lecture and the list stops changing.

steps.action: Tap the primary button to finish onboarding and land on Home.
steps.expected: Home's playlist holds exactly the lectures the Value moment screen listed — same count, same titles.
